title: Repairing a rotten window frame corner with epoxy filler
subtitle: Consolidate and rebuild a softened corner on a timber window frame using a two-part epoxy wood filler without removing the frame
excerpt: How to repair a rotten timber window frame corner using wood consolidant and two-part epoxy filler. Covers removing soft wood, applying consolidant, building up with epoxy filler, shaping to the original profile, and priming.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK trade joinery and wood repair practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A two-part filler system consisting of a resin and a hardener mixed together to form a rigid, waterproof repair material that bonds chemically to timber and can be shaped, sanded, and painted. Two common types: a thick paste for building up missing sections, and a liquid consolidant for pre-treating soft, punky timber before filling.

A low-viscosity resin solution that penetrates deeply into soft or punky timber, binding the fibres together and halting fungal decay. Applied before epoxy filler so the filler bonds to solid, consolidated material rather than to crumbling wood. Sold as a companion product to most two-part epoxy wood fillers.

Use a chisel and utility knife to excavate all the soft, crumbling timber from the repair area. Probe with a bradawl and keep removing material until the tool meets solid resistance. The final cavity must have clean, firm sides. Brush away all dust and debris. The repair only works if every surface the filler bonds to is structurally sound.

Mix and apply the epoxy filler

Mix equal volumes of resin and hardener on a clean board according to the instructions. Work quickly: working time is typically 20 to 30 minutes at room temperature. Press the filler firmly into the cavity, building up in layers no thicker than about 20 mm. Slightly overfill the repair to allow for shaping.

While the filler is still plastic (before full hardening), use the filling knife to shape it to match the surrounding moulding profile. Dipping the blade in water or white spirit helps prevent the filler from sticking to the knife. Once fully hardened, rasp, file, or sand to the final profile. Epoxy filler is very hard when cured and dulls sandpaper quickly: start with coarse abrasive and finish fine. Prime and paint within 24 hours of sanding.

attrs.symptom: Filler falls away from the repair after a few months
attrs.cause: The consolidant had not fully cured before the filler was applied, or soft timber was left in the cavity.
attrs.fix: Remove the failed filler, check the cavity for any remaining soft timber, re-apply consolidant, allow full cure, and re-fill.

attrs.symptom: Filler sets before shaping is complete
attrs.cause: The temperature was higher than expected, shortening the working time.
attrs.fix: Work in smaller batches. If the filler has hardened with the surface proud of the original profile, file and sand back to the correct profile rather than trying to re-work the set material.
